key_insight: Self-powered Se/ZnMgO visual synapses use photon energy to increase or decrease synaptic weight at zero bias.
engineering_relevance: These photodiodes integrate optical sensing, memory and processing, offering a route to low-electrical-power neuromorphic vision on flexible substrates.
method: Apply wavelength-selective light pulses to write and read zero-bias photocurrent states.
Probe interface charge trapping using spectral illumination, reverse-bias erasure and device simulations.
Evaluate measured weight updates and noise in a handwritten-digit recognition network.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 38% potentiation at 365 nm, depression reaching 30% at higher flux, up to 19 levels per branch, and recognition accuracy of 89% without noise and 85% with measured noise versus 97.5% for floating-point weights.
watch_item: The switching crossover depends on interface defects, making defect control important for reproducibility; zero electrical bias does not eliminate optical energy costs.
paper_title: Wavelength-selective bidirectional plasticity in self-powered Se/ZnMgO visual synapses
